    # To determine whether p lies inside the triangle abc or on one of its edges,
    # I use barycentric coordinates.

    # The triangle is defined by the edges a -> b, b -> c, and c -> a.
    # The helper below returns True only when the point q lies on the side
    # from p through r, including the endpoints.
    def on_segment(q, p, r):
        if min(p[0], r[0]) <= q[0] <= max(p[0], r[0]) and min(p[1], r[1]) <= q[1] <= max(p[1], r[1]):
            if p[0] != r[0]:
                return abs((q[1] - p[1]) / (r[1] - p[1]) - (q[0] - p[0]) / (r[0] - p[0])) < 0.00001
            else:
                return q[0] == p[0]

    # A point lies inside or on the triangle exactly when its barycentric coordinates,
    # computed as the areas of the three small triangles formed with the edges, are all >= 0
    # and sum to the area of abc. I do not divide by the large area, so cancelling across
    # all three terms keeps the sign.
    v0x, v0y = b[0] - a[0], b[1] - a[1]
    v1x, v1y = c[0] - a[0], c[1] - a[1]
    v2x, v2y = p[0] - a[0], p[1] - a[1]
    c0 = v0x * v2y - v0y * v2x
    c1 = v1x * v2y - v1y * v2x
    c2 = v0x * v1y - v0y * v1x
    return c0 >= 0 and c1 >= 0 and c2 >= 0 and (c0 + c1 + c2) >= c2

def coffee_machine_credit(events, prices, stock):
    credit = 0
    total = 0
    final_stock = dict(stock)
    for op, value in events:
        if op == "insert":
            credit += value
        elif op == "select":
            name = value
            price = prices.get(name, 0)
            if final_stock.get(name, 0) > 0 and credit >= price:
                final_stock[name] -= 1
                credit -= price
                total += 1
    return credit, final_stock, total
